standard.title: Use vowels and blends to read and write
standard.description: use short vowels, common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs to write words, and blend these to read one- and two-syllable words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can manipulate phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution (AC9E1LY10). They have been developing phoneme-grapheme knowledge at Foundation level. They have not yet applied knowledge of long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs systematically to read and write one- and two-syllable words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use short vowels, common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs to write words, and blend these to read one- and two-syllable words.

nodes.label: Short vowels in words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use short vowel sounds to read and write words with short vowel patterns.
nodes.minimum_width: Read and write at least five single-syllable words using short vowel patterns (a, e, i, o, u).
nodes.typical_width: Apply knowledge of all five short vowel sounds to read and write a range of single-syllable words, including CVC and CVCC patterns.
wider: Compare minimal pairs with different short vowels (e.g. 'man', 'men', 'min', 'mon') and discuss how the vowel changes meaning
Sort words by short vowel sound across five families
nodes.hinge_reason: Short vowel accuracy is foundational for the entire phonics sequence — errors in short vowels produce systematic misreadings that cascade into long vowel work (N2), digraph work (N3) and two-syllable reading (N4).

response_modes.reason: Short vowel accuracy is foundational — errors in short vowels cascade through spelling and decoding. Fluent recognition and production of all five short vowel patterns requires sustained practice.

success_criteria: Student reads single-syllable words with short vowels correctly
Student writes words with short vowels using correct graphemes

nodes.label: Common long vowels
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use common long vowel sounds to read and write words, applying common spelling patterns.
nodes.minimum_width: Read and write at least three words using a common long vowel pattern (e.g. silent-e: 'time', 'make').
nodes.typical_width: Apply common long vowel spelling patterns — silent-e, and other common patterns — to read and write words with long vowel sounds.
wider: Explore that long vowels can be represented by different spelling patterns (e.g. the long /a/ in 'make', 'rain', 'play') — introduce at exposure level
Sort long vowel words by spelling pattern
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who apply short vowel rules to long vowel words produce systematic misreadings — this misconception, if uncorrected, causes persistent errors in reading unfamiliar words with silent-e and other long vowel patterns.

response_modes.reason: Students frequently apply short vowel rules to long vowel words. Encountering long vowels in multiple spelling patterns — even just recognising they exist — helps prevent over-application of the short vowel schema.

success_criteria: Student reads words with a common long vowel pattern correctly
Student applies at least one long vowel spelling pattern in writing

nodes.label: Consonant blends and digraphs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use consonant blends and digraphs to read and write words.
nodes.minimum_width: Read and write at least two words with consonant blends and two words with digraphs.
nodes.typical_width: Apply consonant blend knowledge (initial and final: bl-, st-, cr-, -st, -nd) and common digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh) to read and write single-syllable words.
wider: Compare reading words with blends versus without (e.g. 'rest' vs 'rest' without the -st) to see how blends change meaning
Collect and categorise words by blend or digraph type
success_criteria: Student reads single-syllable words containing consonant blends correctly
Student writes single-syllable words with common digraphs (sh, ch, th) correctly

nodes.label: Reading two-syllable words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can blend phoneme knowledge to read one- and two-syllable words.
nodes.minimum_width: Read at least three two-syllable words by breaking them into syllables and blending.
nodes.typical_width: Apply blending skills to read one- and two-syllable words containing short vowels, long vowels, blends and digraphs, using syllable boundary knowledge to manage two-syllable words.
wider: Read two-syllable compound words and discuss how each syllable carries meaning
Explore how syllable boundaries are determined in two-syllable words

response_modes.reason: Reading two-syllable words requires integrating all prior phonics knowledge — vowel patterns, blends, digraphs — across multiple syllables. It is the integration task that demonstrates applied phonic knowledge.

success_criteria: Student reads a two-syllable word by attempting to break it into syllables
Student correctly reads at least three two-syllable words using phonic knowledge
